content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Columbus

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires specific education and project-management experience to qualify for the PMP®. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—typically a combination of a four-year degree plus documented hours leading projects, or equivalent experience without a degree. Verify your background meets the standard before enrolling in training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP® course. Attend all sessions synchronously from anywhere, interact with active certified practitioners, and cover the full PMBOK® Guide framework. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and prepares you for application and exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, create your PMI account and submit your PMP® application, documenting your project experience and educational background. Pay the associated exam fee through PMI's portal. PMI will audit and approve your application before you can schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor support—to reinforce course material. Schedule your proctored exam when ready. The computer-based test evaluates your mastery of project-management domains; pass to earn your PMP® credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: PMP® certification requires renewal every three years. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) by attending training, volunteering, or contributing to the profession. Stay current with PMI membership and compliance to keep your credential active and competitive in your local job market.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.
